_comment: ALL patient-facing text lives here. It must be reviewed and approved by the radiology team before use. The companion never decides anything medical: it asks, explains approved information and alerts staff.
greeting: Hello, I'm your CT companion. I'll ask you a few short safety questions before your scan, and you can ask me questions at any time. Would you like to continue in English or in German?
start: Thank you. Please answer each question with yes or no. If you're not sure, just say so.
not_understood: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you please answer yes or no?
unsure_ack: No problem. I'll let the staff know so they can check this with you.
detail_prompt: Could you tell me a bit more?
detail_ack: Thank you, I've noted that for the staff.
urgent_reply: I'm calling a member of staff for you right now. Please stay where you are.
unknown_question: That's a good question. I'll pass it on to the staff, and they will answer it for you.

checklist.question: Is there any chance that you could be pregnant?
checklist.ack_yes: Thank you for telling me. The staff will talk with you about this before the scan.

checklist.question: Are you currently breastfeeding?
checklist.ack_yes: Thank you. The staff will tell you if there is anything you need to do.

checklist.question: Have you ever had a reaction to contrast dye, the special dye used for X-ray or CT scans?
Do you have any other allergies, for example to medicines?
Do you have kidney disease, reduced kidney function, or are you on dialysis?
Do you have diabetes, or do you take metformin?
checklist.ack_yes: Thank you. The staff will tell you whether anything changes for your medication. Please don't change it on your own.

checklist.question: Do you have a thyroid condition, for example an overactive thyroid?
Are you taking any regular medication?
Are you in pain, very nervous, or would it be hard for you to lie still for a few minutes?
checklist.ack_yes: Thank you for telling me. The staff will help you get comfortable, and you can talk to them during the scan.

after_checklist: Thank you, that's all my questions.

Before the scan, please remove metal objects such as jewellery, piercings if possible, hairpins and glasses. The staff will tell you if you also need to remove hearing aids or removable dentures. Clothing without metal is best; you may be given a gown.
The scan itself usually takes only a few minutes. You lie on a table that moves slowly through a large open ring. Please lie still and follow the breathing instructions.
If you receive contrast dye, you may feel warm or notice a metallic taste for a moment. That is common. If you feel unwell at any time, tell the staff straight away.
You can ask me a question now, or just wait. A member of staff will come to you.

q: how long does the scan take
faq.a: The scan itself usually takes only a few minutes. With preparation, you may be in the room a little longer.
The scan itself doesn't hurt. If you get contrast dye, you'll feel a small needle prick for the cannula.
A CT scan uses X-rays. Your doctors only request it when the benefit outweighs the small risk, and the dose is kept as low as possible. The staff can answer detailed questions.

q: what does the contrast feel like
faq.a: Contrast dye makes certain organs and blood vessels easier to see. Many people feel warm or notice a metallic taste for a moment. Tell the staff right away if you feel unwell.
Rules about eating and drinking depend on your scan. Please ask the staff, they will tell you exactly.
Your companion can usually wait nearby. The staff will tell you whether they can come into the room.
Clothing without metal is best. You may be asked to change into a gown.

q: when do i get the results
when will i know the results
faq.a: A radiologist looks at your images and sends a report to your doctor, who will discuss the results with you.

q: i am scared of small spaces
faq.a: A CT scanner is a short, open ring, not a long tube, and your head often stays outside. Please tell the staff if you are worried.
Please try to lie still during the scan, because movement can blur the images. The staff will tell you when you may move again.
Please ask the staff, they will tell you what applies to you.
